questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Etymology and Concept of Yoga' refers to.
questions.a: Yoga originates from the Sanskrit root 'Yuj', signifying connection, yoking, or integration of individual self-awareness with higher universal consciousness.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Etymology and Concept of Yoga'.
questions.a: Achieving unified consciousness and balance between physical existence and mental state.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Etymology and Concept of Yoga', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Yoga = Union (Body + Mind + Spirit)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Historical Epochs of Yoga' refers to.
questions.a: The historical evolution of yogic philosophy structured across six major ages, spanning over 5000 years from ancient seals to contemporary worldwide recognition.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Historical Epochs of Yoga'.
questions.a: Systematic transition of yogic practices from early civilization seals to international wellness adoption.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Historical Epochs of Yoga', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: History = Pre-Vedic + Vedic/Upanishadic + Classical + Post-Classical + Modern + Contemporary

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Astanga Yoga (Eight Limbs)' refers to.
questions.a: A comprehensive eight-stage framework designed by Maharshi Patanjali to regulate mental fluctuations and achieve complete spiritual absorption.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Astanga Yoga (Eight Limbs)'.
questions.a: Sequential progression from social ethics and personal purity to internal meditative absorption.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Astanga Yoga (Eight Limbs)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Astanga = Yama + Niyama + Asana + Pranayama + Pratyahara + Dharana + Dhyana + Samadhi

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Panchamahavrata and Eightfold Path' refers to.
questions.a: Ethical codes established by Mahavira (Five Great Vows) and Buddha (Eightfold Path) that served as early spiritual guidelines integral to yogic sadhana.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Panchamahavrata and Eightfold Path'.
questions.a: Moral restraint and balanced cognitive conduct form the bedrock of self-discipline in yoga.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Panchamahavrata and Eightfold Path', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Ethical Practice = Panchamahavrata (Jain Vows) + Atthangika Magga (Buddhist Path)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Traditional Schools of Yoga' refers to.
questions.a: Distinct philosophical streams and lineages that provide specialized pathways toward self-realization suited to different human temperaments.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Traditional Schools of Yoga'.
questions.a: Multiple complementary paths catering to intellect, devotion, selfless work, mental discipline, and body-energy balance.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Traditional Schools of Yoga', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Yoga Schools = Jnana + Bhakti + Karma + Patanjala + Hatha

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Three Stages of Jnana Yoga' refers to.
questions.a: A triadic method of intellectual inquiry consisting of listening to truth, logical reflection, and deep meditative assimilation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Three Stages of Jnana Yoga'.
questions.a: Transforming theoretical wisdom into direct realization through reflection and sustained meditation.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Three Stages of Jnana Yoga', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Jnana Stages = Sravana + Manana + Nididhyasana

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Navadha Bhakti (Ninefold Devotion)' refers to.
questions.a: Nine progressive devotional practices designed to direct emotions toward the divine and dissolve egoistic barriers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Navadha Bhakti (Ninefold Devotion)'.
questions.a: Refinement of human emotions through nine distinct devotional expressions.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Navadha Bhakti (Ninefold Devotion)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Navadha Bhakti = 9 Devotional Practices

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Panchakosha (Five Sheaths of Existence)' refers to.
questions.a: The Taittiriya Upanishad model describing human existence across five concentric sheaths from outer physical matter to inner bliss.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Panchakosha (Five Sheaths of Existence)'.
questions.a: Multi-layered framework connecting physical structure, energetic force, mental thoughts, higher wisdom, and pure bliss.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Panchakosha (Five Sheaths of Existence)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Existence = Annamaya + Pranamaya + Manomaya + Vijnanamaya + Anandamaya

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Yoga for Holistic Health' refers to.
questions.a: A comprehensive healthcare framework that establishes harmony across physical, cognitive, emotional, social, and spiritual dimensions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Yoga for Holistic Health'.
questions.a: Treating root causes of disease to maintain internal equilibrium (homeostasis) and mental calmness.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Yoga for Holistic Health', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Holistic Health = Physical + Cognitive + Emotional + Social + Spiritual Wellbeing

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Categories of Yogic Practices' refers to.
questions.a: A structured system of practical techniques including detoxification, body alignments, breath regulation, energy control, and silent meditation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Categories of Yogic Practices'.
questions.a: A versatile toolkit of mental and physical disciplines designed for personal wellness and self-realization.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Categories of Yogic Practices', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Practices = Kriya + Surya Namaskara + Asana + Pranayama + Bandha/Mudra + Dhyana
